hook_text: Every day, thousands of containers move through one bay on the KwaZulu-Natal coast. Without it, Gauteng would grind to a halt.
clip_script: The Port of Durban sits in a calm bay behind the Bluff, a long green ridge of dunes. Sand keeps drifting into the entrance, so dredgers dig it out, again and again. Through that entrance come container ships from Asia, tankers full of fuel and car carriers. Gantry cranes lift box after box, close to three million TEUs in a busy year. South African-made cars roll onto ships for Europe. Sugar pours into bulk carriers. Then it all heads inland: trucks up the N3, trains to City Deep in Johannesburg, fuel through a pipeline. When the port slows down, prices rise and jobs suffer across southern Africa.
visual_style: A whiteboard cross-section of the bay with the Bluff, a dredger at the entrance, labelled terminals for containers, cars, fuel and sugar, and lines running inland to Gauteng.
pacing: Fast, rhythmic tour of the terminals, slower close on why it matters.
